---
title: "Before the day"
---
Before the day you read the case study and check that the browser lab loads on the machine that you will bring, which takes about an hour. The day is worked mainly in the browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser, with the data already in place, so there is nothing that you have to install. Installing R, an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.) and the downloadable workspace is optional and takes longer, but this is the format that uses them most. Part 2 has a stretch on the IDE and Part 4 one on the report, and with the workspace you work through both on your own machine rather than following them on the shared screen.

## 1. The case study

[Read the case study](../../cases/housing/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The case study presents the original study and its design, SCORE and the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses and the question that each of them answered, how their results were put on one scale, and the replication with new data. Every part of the day works on this case.

## 2. The browser lab

[Open the browser lab at Task 1](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-1-setup){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Open the lab once on the machine and in the browser that you will use, wait until the first cell shows a "Run Code" button, and run the setup cell of Task 1. If it does not load, try another browser, and tell the facilitator before the day.

## 3. R and the workspace (recommended)

[Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

This step is optional, and recommended for this day. Install R and an IDE, download the workspace zip, and run `R/check_setup.R` until it prints OK. You do this once. The [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met.

## 4. Your IDE (optional)

[Read the module on the IDEs](../../companion/ide.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The companion module on the three IDEs shows where the console, the variables and the data viewer are in the IDE that you chose, and what changes between the three.

**By the start of the day** you have the browser lab loading on the machine that you will use, or the workspace working if you installed it, and you know what the claim is and who the five Multi100 analysts were.
